# Tobit Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_003_page_001.jpg

---

**3:1** And I-was-grieved and I-wept and I-prayed in-grief, saying:

**3:2** "Righteous [art] you, O Lord, and all your works and all your ways [are] mercy and truth and true judgment you-judge for-the-age.

**3:3** And now, O Lord, remember me and look-upon me; do-not-punish me for my sins and for my ignorances and for [those of] my fathers, who sinned before-you.

**3:4** For they disobeyed your commandments and you-gave us over to plundering and to captivity and to death and to a-proverb of-reproach for all-the nations among whom we-have-been-scattered.

**3:5** And now many [are] your judgments, [which are] true, in-dealing-with me according-to my sins and those-of my fathers, because we-did-not do your commandments, for we-did-not walk in-truth before-you.

**3:6** And now, deal-with me according-to-what-is-pleasing before-you; command my spirit to-be-taken up, that I-may-be-released and may-become earth; for it-is-better for-me to-die than to-live, because false reproaches I-have-heard, and great [is] the-grief in-me. Command, O Lord, that I-be-released from this distress; let-me-depart to the-eternal place; do-not-turn-away your-face from-me, O Lord. For it-is-better for-me to-die than to-see great distress in-my life and to-hear reproaches."

**3:7** On that same day it-also-happened to-Sarah the-daughter of Raguel in-Ecbatana of-Media that she-also heard reproaches from one-of the maidservants of her-father,

**3:8** because she-had-been-given in-marriage to seven husbands and Asmodeus the-evil demon had-killed them before they-had-been-with her as-it-is-customary-for men. And the-maidservant said to-her: "You yourself are-the-one-killing your husbands. See, you-have-been-given to seven husbands and have-not-been-called by the-name of any of-them.

**3:9** Why do-you beat us? Because your husbands are-dead? Go with them! Let-there-not-be seen from-you son or daughter for-the-age."

**3:10** On that day she-was-grieved and she-wept and she-went-up to-the upper-room of her father to hang herself. But she-reconsidered and said: "Lest they reproach my father and say to-him: 'There-was to-you one beloved daughter and she-hanged herself from distress.' And I-will-bring my father's old-age down into grief into Hades. It-is-better for-me not to-hang-myself but to-pray to-the Lord that I-may-die and may-hear no-longer reproaches in-my life."

**3:11** At that hour she-stretched-out [her] hands toward the-window and she-prayed and said: "Blessed [art] you, O Lord my God, and blessed [is] your holy and glorious name for-the-ages; let all your works bless you for-the-ages.

**3:12** And now, O Lord, I-set my eyes and my face toward you.

**3:13** Say [the word] that I-be-released from-the earth and that I-hear no-longer reproach.

**3:14** You know, O Lord, that I-am pure from all sin of a-man,

**3:15** and that I-have-not defiled my name nor the-name of my-father in-the land of my-captivity. I-am the only-begotten of my-father and there-is not to-him another child to-be his-heir, nor a brother near-of-kin nor a relative-by-marriage belonging-to-him for whom I-should-keep myself as-a-wife. Already seven husbands of-mine have-died; why should I-live? And if it-is-not pleasing to-you to-kill me, O Lord, look-upon my reproach."

**3:16** At that hour the-prayer of both-of-them was-heard before the-glory of God the Great.

**3:17** And Raphael was-sent to-heal both-of-them: Tobit, to-remove the-white-films from his-eyes that he-might-see with his eyes the-light of God; and Sarah the-daughter of Raguel to-give to Tobias the-son of Tobit as-a-wife and to-bind Asmodeus the-evil demon, because it-fell-by-lot to Tobias to-inherit her before all-the-others who-were-desiring to-take-her. At-that-time Tobit returned from-the courtyard into his-house and Sarah the-daughter of Raguel came-down from-the upper-room.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

- 3:2: The doxology opening Tobit's prayer is a standard liturgical formula. "True judgment you judge for the age" — the Greek krineis eis ton aiōna is "you judge unto the age/forever"; EMET preserves the eschatological force.
- 3:3: "ignorances" (agnoiai) — sins of unknowing, as distinct from willful sins. The word appears in the LXX to translate Hebrew shegagot. The distinction between willed and unwilled transgression is a specifically Semitic legal-theological category.
- 3:4: "a proverb of reproach" (parabolēn oneidismou) — to become a byword among the nations; cf. Deut 28:37.
- 3:6: The repetition "it is better for me to die" occurs twice in the verse; EMET preserves both occurrences as the Greek text has them.
- 3:7: "Ecbatana of Media" — the capital of Media; modern Hamadan, Iran.
- 3:8: "Asmodeus the evil demon" (Asmodaios ho daimonion to ponēron) — the name is the GII form; derived from Avestan Aēšma-daēva, the demon of wrath. This is the only occurrence of Asmodeus in canonical/deuterocanonical Scripture.
- 3:10: The upper room (hyperōon) is where women withdrew for lamentation; Sarah's choosing it for suicide and then for prayer is deliberate spatial symbolism.
- 3:15: "only-begotten" (monogenēs) — the same word used for an only child of either gender. Note later NT usage; EMET preserves the literal term.
- 3:16: "before the glory of God the Great" — GII unique phrase; the shorter recension simply has "before God."
- 3:17: The divine appointment of Raphael and the lot-casting (eklērothe) are grammatically compressed in the Greek; EMET renders the syntax as literally as possible.

*— EMET*
